text:
kai: seeing a weird sawtooth pattern of DNS resolve times from model-serving pods in eastus-gpu-pool. some requests spike to 1.2s then back to 20ms repeatedly. impacts internal service calls to metadata and model-config endpoints.

maria: interesting — did this start after the morning network deploy?

kai: yeah around the kube-proxy iptables roll this morning. also noticed more UDP timeouts in coredns logs.

ash: can you paste a sample of the dig/traceroute? want to see if UDP vs TCP differs.

kai: pasted below:
```
; dig +time=2 @10.0.0.10 metadata.svc.cluster.local A
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 0, ADDITIONAL: 1
;; QUESTION SECTION:
;metadata.svc.cluster.local.
;; Query time: 1209 msec
;; SERVER: 10.0.0.10#53(10.0.0.10)
; (time out over UDP)\n
; dig +tcp +time=2 @10.0.0.10 metadata.svc.cluster.local A
;; Query time: 28 msec
```

julian: that pattern screams MTU/frag or intermittent packet loss on UDP path. TCP falls back and is fine. any RDMA-enabled nodes in that pool? RDMA can interact badly with mtu clamping.

kai: some of the older p4d nodes have IB and RDMA settings enabled. but the spike hits both rdma and non-rdma nodes. odd.

maria: could be node-local-dns instances getting evicted or thrashing cache entries. when node-local restarts, queries hit coredns and you see different latency. check kube events for dns-daemonset churn.

ash: I just checked: node-local-dns (dns-cache) pods on node-az-3 restarted 3x between 10:02 and 10:10. logs show 'watch closed: too old resource version' and then a flurry of DNS lookups.

ops-runner: kubectl get events --namespace=kube-system | grep node-local-dns
```
10:02:11 kubelet NodeNotReady node/az-3 status is now: NodeNotReady
10:02:13 Pod node-local-dns-az-3 evicted
10:03:01 Pod node-local-dns-az-3 created
```

julian: NodeNotReady around the same time — could be network egress flap. any MTU mismatches after the iptables change? we did apply an MTU clamp on calico last week.

kai: calico MTU was set to 1500 -> we rolled to 1450 in that patch. some hosts still on 1500.

maria: mixed MTU across nodes + RDMA path = recipe for UDP fragmentation and drops. UDP fragments when payload > path MTU, and fragments are often dropped by intermediate devices.

ash: quick mitigation: switch node-local-dns to prefer TCP for DNS queries to coredns, at least until we reconcile MTU and node upgrade. node-resolver supports TCP fallback.

kai: making a canary change to node-local-dns config to set upstreamTransport: tcp for the az-3 daemonset@kai. will monitor.

ash: also open a ticket to reconcile MTU across the fleet and ensure RDMA interfaces are excluded from calico mtu clamping. julian can you take ownership?

julian: on it. I'll coordinate with eng-infra and hw-ops to standardize MTU to 1450 across gpu pools and push a controlled reboot window for stale 1500 nodes.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-483 — "Intermittent DNS UDP drops eastus GPU nodes" (priority P2). Assigned to eng-infra. Link: https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-2026-483

ops-runner: if folks want quick triage commands: 
```
# check for fragmentation/dropped UDP
sudo tc -s qdisc show dev eth0
# view iptables conntrack drop counters
sudo conntrack -L | grep DNS
```

maria: after switching to TCP upstream we saw query times drop to ~30ms in the canary. please monitor for 15m and capture coredns UDP/dnsmasq counters.

kai: can confirm canary improved error rates on model-service health checks from 6% -> 0.7%. rolling to other nodes in az-3 now.

julian: plan: (1) finish node-local-dns TCP fallback roll (2) schedule MTU reconcile and reboot of 1500 nodes in gpu pools (3) add a calico policy to avoid altering RDMA-enabled interfaces (4) postmortem and metric dashboards for DNS UDP error rate.

ash: adding a quick alert: DNS UDP timeout rate > 1% for 5m -> page oncall until mitigated.

kai: thanks all. will keep thread updated with metrics + logs. :thumbsup:
